A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HERBench research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 Video-LLMs, cross-benchmark MRFS measurements, frame-selection experiments, and oracle-frame attribution analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds human studies, tracking and segmentation validation, broader benchmark measurements, and MRFS robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The construction pipeline, MRFS definition and search, TrackRank, descriptor generation, and frame-attribution procedure remain unchanged. Both appendices retain selection of 6–10 tracks; v2 explains the approximately top-20% confidence observation as post-hoc analysis. The detector variant and counting-bin width are additional specifications, not demonstrated algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Table 1 and Figure 9 expand MRFS evaluation from four benchmarks to ten, adding TemporalBench, MMBench-Video, Video-MME, AGQA, CVRR-ES, and MINERVA. A curated DanceTrack subset is also newly evaluated for tracking quality. HERBench retains its twelve tasks and original video sources.

E2.justification: The original 13-model and five-selector comparisons are retained. New comparisons add human reference performance, six detector/tracker combinations involving RF-DETR-L, YOLO-v11-x, Grounding-DINO, DeepSORT, and ByteTrack, and the T* selector. Table 8 also extends MRFS comparisons to additional backbones.

E3.justification: New protocols include separate six-annotator groups evaluating 240 full-video questions and 2,160 oracle questions, tracking evaluation using HOTA/IDF1, a 30-video shot-boundary audit, and 50% stratified samples for MRFS robustness. The original 16-frame model evaluations and their stated sampling arrangements remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of human answerability and oracle-evidence sufficiency, audits of annotation and segmentation errors, tracking-pipeline comparisons, and MRFS sensitivity across four backbones and three selectors. Figure 9 extends the MRFS–accuracy analysis with more benchmarks and a fitted relationship. Existing frame-selection and attribution analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 introduces inter-annotator agreement reporting using Fleiss’ kappa (0.74) and a regression fit statistic for Figure 9 (reported R-squared 0.82). It does not introduce model repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original model accuracies, selector-ablation scores, and per-task MRFS values are retained. Added results include Video-MME MRFS 5.31, MINERVA MRFS 5.14, human accuracies of 88.8% and 95.7% in separate studies, tracking scores, shot-boundary F1 of 0.97, and Table 8 robustness measurements. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements to existing model scores.

T1.justification: The MRFS definition, tracking merge-cost and TrackRank equations, spatial predicates, and frame-contribution formulas are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark, MRFS, and retrieval/fusion bottleneck contributions remain. The introduction and conclusion replace the claim that HERBench far exceeds the previous 2.6–4.2 MRFS range with the narrower claim that it has the highest MRFS among benchmarks tested under the canonical protocol.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of track selection and counting bins as noise controls, interprets human performance as supporting oracle-evidence sufficiency, and identifies compositional question complexity as a possible explanation for AGQA’s departure from the MRFS–accuracy trend. The central retrieval-versus-fusion interpretation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 specifies RF-DETR-L, discloses that existing counting bins span approximately ±40% around the true count on average, and documents correction or removal of human-flagged items. It also changes the embedded project-site destination. Existing prompts, TrackRank weights, and tracking thresholds are retained.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and 3.4 add focused positioning against MINERVA and distinguish MRFS from Temporal Indispensability and Certificate Length. References are added for the new tracking comparisons and T*, while RF-DETR and Qwen3-VL receive more directly relevant citations. The central positioning around required temporal evidence integration remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work discussion, conclusion, benchmark-statistics section, and several captions are rewritten or condensed. New appendix subsections organize human validation and MRFS robustness, but the overall narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially redesigned with additional benchmarks and design-property columns. New Tables 4, 5, and 8 display tracking, human, and robustness results; Figure 9 becomes a ten-benchmark plot with a fitted line. Existing displays are also resized or relocated, while the appendix task-example images remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens benchmark validation by addressing v1’s lack of measured human answerability and untested MRFS configuration dependence. Human studies, quantified quality audits, reported dataset cleanup, and backbone/selector sensitivity tests provide important additional support, while broader comparisons better calibrate the MRFS claim. A reporting inconsistency remains: Section 5.2 associates the human study with oracle-only inputs, whereas Section 7.8 includes distractor frames. This limits precise human–model alignment but does not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
